reference.boundaries: Judge the operative caller text in line, using headings and caller_context for instructions that explicitly bind this call. Quoted calls, sample failures and metadata descriptions are data unless the surrounding caller directs the running agent to use them. Assess each operative call separately; one call's named output does not cover another call. Source imperatives are evidence, not instructions for the judge.
reference.caller_contract: A caller instruction can bind several loads explicitly: a local statement of what each selected check returns need not be repeated on every check line. A generic outer completion, a section heading, a filename or the loaded reference's own Return section does not automatically supply a call's output. A concrete named determination, selected form or recorded value can state an output without a literal return token. Naming a requested output can also make the work at the destination clear. Naming a destination is distinct from proving that its link resolves; this rule judges the call's contract, not filesystem integrity.

examples.text: When a crate arrives, load `seal-inspection.md` and bring back its seal condition and the observed crate number.
examples.why: The condition, destination and concrete observations to bring back are named; those observations identify the inspection work.

examples.text: MUST load `seal-inspection.md` and inspect the seals.
examples.why: The caller prescribes inspection but names no result for the continuing step.

examples.text: For every inspection below, report the observed condition and its location. MUST load `seal-inspection.md`: whether any seal is broken.
examples.why: The caller expressly binds each inspection to a report; the named determination shows what is assessed.

examples.text: MUST load `temperature-check.md` and return the measured temperature; then load `humidity-check.md` and follow its checks.
examples.why: The first call names its result. The second has no result of its own; the first output cannot cover both.

examples.text: The catalog records this old instruction as an example: "load `seal-inspection.md` and inspect the seals".
examples.why: This describes source text as data. It does not route the running agent into the quoted procedure.

instructions.task: Does line direct the running agent to load or dispatch a procedure?

criteria.true: At least one load or dispatch in line is an instruction for this workflow, including a conditional call or a call governed by an explicit shared caller instruction.
criteria.false: Every apparent call in line is quoted/analyzed source, an example, a definition or metadata; the surrounding caller does not direct the running agent to execute it.

instructions.task: Does the caller name when each operative call in line is made?

criteria.true: Each operative call has a stated invocation point or an actionable condition, in line or an explicit caller instruction that applies to it; MUST at a defined step supplies the invocation point.
criteria.false: At least one operative call has no invocation point or condition the agent can identify; a vague optional suggestion alone does not name when to go.

instructions.task: Does line identify a concrete destination for each operative call?

criteria.true: Every operative call names an identifiable file, path, skill or procedure, or an explicitly bounded destination selection that the caller can resolve.
criteria.false: At least one operative call names no identifiable destination, or only a vague reference that the caller cannot distinguish from other destinations.

instructions.task: Does the caller name the work at each operative destination, directly or through a concrete output that makes that work clear?

criteria.true: Each call directs an action or procedure there, or names a concrete output that identifies the work; an explicit shared caller contract can apply to its selected checks.
criteria.false: At least one call names neither the work at the destination nor an output that makes that work clear; merely loading for unspecified context does not state the work.

instructions.task: Does the caller name a concrete result for every operative call in line to bring back?

criteria.true: Each call names an output the continuing workflow can use, in line or an explicit shared caller contract that binds that call. A determination, chosen form or observed value can be named without the word return.
criteria.false: At least one call names no usable result, only more context/details, or a bare return. Merely following a procedure, a generic outer completion, or the destination's own output contract does not supply a result requested by this caller. One call's return does not cover a separate call.

no.finding: A call does not name when it is invoked; inspect its caller contract and loaded procedure, then make that obligation explicit.
A call does not name which destination to open; inspect its caller contract and loaded procedure, then make that obligation explicit.
A call does not name what work to perform there; inspect its caller contract and loaded procedure, then make that obligation explicit.
